questions.q: Why do you never notice the blank area your blind spot creates?
a: Your brain invents the missing information for you
Your eyes blink often enough to hide the gap
Your retina has a second layer of cells there
Your brain receives the image twice, once per eye
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the brain guesses what belongs in the blank and adds it to the picture.

questions.q: How does the brain usually store a good evening that ended badly?
a: It exaggerates the bad ending and recalls the night as bad
It balances the good and bad parts evenly
It slowly deletes the bad ending over time
It keeps only the single best moment of the evening
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the party example to show memory weighting the ending more heavily than the rest.

questions.q: How does Gilbert say you should judge whether a purchase is worth it?
a: By the value you get for the money compared with other uses
By comparing the price with what you used to pay
By comparing the price with what other shops charge
By comparing the quality with the brand's reputation
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to think about what else the money could buy instead of comparing prices.

questions.q: In the marriage thought experiment, which outcome do people regret more?
a: Not marrying the person who later becomes a billionaire
Marrying the person who later becomes a pyromaniac
Both outcomes equally, since neither can be undone
Neither, because regret fades quickly either way
questions.why: Lesson 3 says people kick themselves over the life they never had, not the bad one they lived.

questions.q: Why can the brain cope with a bad experience better than a missed one?
a: It can find positives in what happened but not in what never did
It forgets painful events faster than neutral ones
It compares real events against imagined ones
It treats inaction as the safer default choice
questions.why: Lesson 3 says it is hard to imagine anything good about an experience you never had.
